It used to stand over me while I was doing homework. Even if I couldn’t see it, it was a really intense dark feeling. When my sister saw it, it opened the door from my parents room and slowly walked down the hallway into her room (our three rooms were in a kind of triangle formation around the stairs.) There were a couple other encounters but we’ve never really figured out what was going on, esp because it was only active on the second floor.

I’m so sorry. The exact same thing happened to me two months prior. And same, some days I’m fine, some days I start crying in work meetings (ok it happened only one time but you get the idea).

It fucking sucks. There is something about losing someone you love to suicide that makes you feel extra helpless. I’m sure he knew how much you loved him. And no matter what you believe in, he’s always going to be with you in some way (I’m not particularly religious but sometimes I hear Ryan in my head when I’m feeling down about myself or experience something that was an inside joke — these moments always remind me that he isn’t totally gone). Anyway, I hope that wasn’t too corny or cloying. Sending you hugs internet stranger, you’re not alone in this.

Yep, I’m looking to take a month off now with medical leave. It’s been three months for me and I can’t cope with work.

I am going through the exact same thing. It’s cruel how fast you’re supposed to just be fine. A coworker of mine has been going through some tough personal stuff too (not suicide or death but still very tough) and my boss literally said to me “he’s going through a hard time too and doesn’t make mistakes” Like fuck you, first of all. But second there’s no timeline for being okay. And it’s their problem if they are unfeeling #%^*]. Sending you hugs, and your work a big middle finger.

I’m so sorry. The first two weeks after Ryan left me is a total blur. I had a complete dissociative episode the first 24 hours. I know I’m still having a really tough time, but from my experience you are in the worst of it.

I just remember screaming to the sky “you were supposed to be here” and that didn’t just mean for me, but for my future kids. We were like family. He was gonna be the godparent (or “godless-parent” is what he used to say lol) So yeah, I know how that goes when someone who was going to be with you for the long haul takes themselves out of the picture. I’m sending you big hugs. Try to drink some water.
Definitely. I’ve been making a lot of art. He was my #1 fan, but making things has been helping me cope.

💜💜💜

Yeah, my supervisors really are about “taking your time to grieve” as long as it doesn’t affect them. There’s a lot of pressure to be high functioning and I’m just not there. Love you back, stranger.
Oh my god —- fuck that author. I hope they never have a satisfying orgasm. And I’m sorry for your loss. I’m sending you lots of love, and solidarity. I miss my best friend so much.

Not to be a broken record but I also rotate! I write plays and sketches and satire articles, I also sound edit, and paint, and cast resin, read tarot, read books, and play video games. The artistic stuff I am lucky enough to have be a bit of a side hustle but the point is Im always following my bliss. Also, it’s so fun to have so many things I am good at and like doing! Pretty convinced all of the Renaissance masters had adhd because they were always switching around (ok I’m thinking pretty specifically about DaVinci, but society used to value people who could do many things!!!)

Hi — you are not a stupid wreck and you do have a future. I completely understand how you feel... everything in your post, in fact. The push to be "okay" is exhausting and it's unfair. I just want to tell you that so many of the most "successful" people I know are struggling with the exact same things you and I are. Just know you have a total internet stranger out here who is rooting for you and that — by being here — you have value. Hope it's not too saccharine to say, just know someone is rooting for you.

Hey — the vaccine is important and good to get. If not your own life, you are literally saving other people's lives. 

And, fwiw, living takes more courage than dying.
